章节.概要:
東京23区内にある旅客営業路線では京成金町線・西武豊島線と並んで数少ない全線単線路線である。また、東武鉄道の路線の中では鬼怒川線と同様に、同一の都道府県かつ単一の市町村内で全線が完結する路線である。

この路線は、西板線（伊勢崎線西新井駅 - 東上本線上板橋駅間 11.6 km）計画のうち用地確保が完了した区間にて、西新井大師（総持寺）参詣者の輸送を目的として1931年に開業した。1968年の環七通り拡幅の際に線路用地の一部を提供したため、営業キロが100 m短縮され1 kmとなり、1991年には西新井駅近辺を除き高架化されたため、東武鉄道では唯一、踏切が全線において一つも存在しない路線となった。

途中駅は無い。大師前駅には自動改札機・自動券売機・自動精算機は設置されておらず（入口にその旨が掲示されている）、同駅の乗車券発売や改札などの機能は、西新井駅構内の乗り換え通路上に大師前駅からの乗車券が購入出来る券売機や連絡専用の自動改札機を設置して対応している。よって、大師前駅からは、定期券乗車客や企画切符乗車客以外は有効な乗車券を持たずに乗ることになる。

他に同様の形態をとる駅としては、名鉄築港線の東名古屋港駅や山陽本線（和田岬線）の和田岬駅・阪神武庫川線の洲先駅・東鳴尾駅が挙げられる。

章节.歴史:
1924年（大正13年）5月5日：鉄道免許状下付（南足立郡西新井村-北豊島郡上板橋村間 動力蒸気）。

 1945年（昭和20年）5月20日：全線営業休止。
 1947年（昭和22年）5月21日：全線営業再開。大師線と改称。
 1968年（昭和43年）12月1日：環七通り拡幅のため大師前駅移転。0.1 km短縮。

 2003年（平成15年）3月19日：ワンマン運転開始。

2003年からはワンマン化され、通常は2両編成の8000系（ワンマン対応車）1本が西新井駅と大師前駅の間を往復している。ほぼ終日に渡り10分間隔、例外となる早朝深夜時間帯も最大15分間隔で運行されている。

原則として西新井駅では1番線を使用するが、出入庫時に使用する本線への線路と接続の関係で、昼過ぎの1往復は車両交換のため2番線を使用する（1番線は本線の線路とは接続されていない）。車両は亀戸線と共通運用のため、亀戸線で朝ラッシュのみ運用される車両が運用終了後に亀戸駅2番線に留置され、昼過ぎに西新井駅まで回送されて大師線の運用に入るダイヤとなっている。

正月などの多客時には、通常は車両交換の際にのみ使用される西新井駅2番線を使用して、2本運転が実施される。

章节.西板線計画:
第二次世界大戦前には西新井駅 - 東上本線上板橋駅間を結ぶ西板線の計画が立てられていた。1920年の東武鉄道・東上鉄道合併により、東武本線系統との接続を図る目的であった。

ほぼ現在の環七通りに沿って途中に大師前・鹿浜・神谷・板橋上宿（いずれも仮称）の各駅が計画され、1922年11月に南足立郡西新井村（西新井駅） - 北豊島郡上板橋村（上板橋駅）間の免許申請が行われ、1924年5月に免許が下付された。

だが、申請から免許下付までの間に発生した関東大震災による既存路線の被災復旧を優先したこと、当時建設中だった荒川放水路の堤防などの護岸整備が完了しておらず架橋の設計ができないこと、荒川放水路と隅田川を跨ぐ橋梁の建設費用の問題、予定地の町関係者からの経路変更要求への対応画策などの問題が起こり、その対応に忙殺されているうちに、大正末期から昭和初期にかけて路線予定地が急速に市街地化されたため「建設費が高額となり、採算の見込みがない」との理由で、西新井 - 大師前間開業の翌年、1932年に鹿浜 - 上板橋間の起業を廃止した。大師前 - 鹿浜間については「工事竣工期限延期願」を関係省庁に提出していたが、1937年6月に不認可とされ、免許が失効した。

この計画中止について『東武鉄道六十五年史』では「遂にその線の実現を見るに至らなかったことは、交通網の現状から考えてまことに残念なことであった」と記されている。

西板線は東上線系ではなく本線系とする計画であり、両路線群間の車両転属回送経路としても活用する計画であったが、未成となったことで、東武悲願の「本線系と東上線系路線との接続」はならなかった。この西板線が未成に終わったことから、両系統路線群を接続する自社路線がないため、東上線と本線・野田線との間で車両を輸送する場合は秩父鉄道秩父本線が使われている。

西板線の線形は、東上線の下り方（寄居方面）と伊勢崎線の上り方（浅草方面）とを直通運行する際に折り返しがないように計画された。上板橋駅の上り方に、東上線からの分岐予定地および貨物操車場予定地として買収した土地は、起業廃止後常盤台住宅地として分譲されることになり、そのアクセス駅として武蔵常盤駅（現・ときわ台駅）が設置された。

英文.首段: Daishimae Station (大師前駅, Daishimae-eki) is a railway station on the Tobu Daishi Line in Adachi, Tokyo, Japan, operated by the private railway operator Tobu Railway. Its station number is TS 51.

章节.History:
Opened on 20 December 1931 (Showa 6) as a station on the Nishi-Itabashi Line. It was the first-phase section of the planned Nishi-Itabashi Line connecting Nishi-Arai and Kami-Itabashi stations. Initially two-car trains ran through directly from Asakusa-Kaminarimon Station (present-day Asakusa Station).
- 20 May 1945 (Showa 20): Services suspended.
- 21 May 1947 (Showa 22): Services resumed; following a renaming of the line, the station became part of the Daishi Line.
- 1 December 1968 (Showa 43): Relocated due to the widening of Ring Road 7 (Kanpachi-dori).
- 26 July 1991 (Heisei 3): The station was elevated using a temporary station building.
- 17 March 2012 (Heisei 24): Station number "TS 51" introduced.
- 27 March 2015 (Heisei 27): A departure melody was introduced.
章节.Station layout:
The station is elevated with a single side platform serving one track. Structurally it could be configured as an island platform serving two tracks, but the northern track bed has been covered over so as to be flush with the platform, giving the platform a generous width for the station's scale.
The departure melody "Passenger" is used.
An elevator and an up-only escalator connect the ground level with the platform. A station building housing tenants such as a clinic adjoins the station. Tobu Bus Central's Nishi-Arai depot is located within the station premises, including the space beneath the elevated tracks.
Before relocation, the station stood south of the present site, just across the Ring Road 7 crossing; it was a European-style building lined with arched entrances. In its ground-level era it had a bay-platform layout with separate boarding and alighting platforms.
章节.Features:
Apart from tram lines and new transit systems, this is a rare unstaffed station within the 23 wards of Tokyo. It is also the busiest unstaffed station on the Tobu Railway network.
There are no automatic ticket gates, automatic ticket vending machines, or fare-adjustment machines on site, and notices to that effect are posted at the entrance. Functions such as ticket sales and ticket checking for this station are handled at the transfer passage inside Nishi-Arai Station, where ticket vending machines selling tickets from this station and dedicated inter-station automatic gates are installed. Other stations operating in a similar manner include Higashi-Nagoya Port Station on the Meitetsu Chikkō Line and Wada-Misaki Station on the Sanyo Main Line (Wada-Misaki Branch).
The ticket window is normally closed with a shutter. During periods when many worshippers visit Nishi-Arai Daishi, such as the New Year season, staff are stationed there to sell tickets. A staffed ticket-checking booth (latch) is also provided, but it is not used even during busy periods because Nishi-Arai Station has automatic gates.
章节.Usage: In fiscal 2021, the station had an average of 11,275 boarding and alighting passengers daily. After the Nippori-Toneri Liner opened to the west of the station in 2008 and stations such as Nishi-Arai-Daishi opened, some passengers shifted to that line, and ridership in recent years has fallen to roughly half its peak.
章节.Surrounding area: Close by is Nishi-Arai Daishi (Soji-ji), from which the station takes its name.
章节.Bus routes: The nearest bus stops are "Nishi-Arai-Daishi", "Nishi-Arai-Daishi-mae", and "Nishi-Arai-Shako". Route buses are operated by Tobu Bus Central, Kokusai Kogyo, and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation (Toei Bus).
章节.Other: The Nippori-Toneri Liner, which opened on 30 March 2008, has "Nishi-Arai-Daishi Station" on Oku-Ohashi Street. It lies about 1.7 km from this station, and this station remains the closer one for access to Nishi-Arai Daishi.

Nishi-Arai Station (西新井駅, Nishi-Arai-eki) is a railway station in Adachi, Tokyo, Japan, operated by the private railway operator Tobu Railway. Its station number is TS 13.
The station is served by the Isesaki Line (Skytree Line) and the Daishi Line. The section of the Isesaki Line on either side of this station forms part of the "Tobu Skytree Line" nickname section, and the Daishi Line starts at this station.

章节.Chronology:
27 August 1899 (Meiji 32): Opened simultaneously with the opening of the Tobu Railway section between Kita-Senju and Kuki.
15 December 1966 (Showa 41): At around 22:37, train 2306D bound for Nishi-Arai from Daishimae and train 2155S (Eidan 3000 series) departing Nishi-Arai collided inside Nishi-Arai Station. Seven passengers were killed, four seriously injured, and sixteen slightly injured.
23 November 1973 (Showa 48): The station building complex "Tosca Nishi-kan" opened.
21 April 1981 (Showa 56): "Tosca Higashi-kan" opened.
31 March 2005 (Heisei 17): Elevators between the ticket gates and the platforms entered service. Barrier-free toilets were newly installed at gate level, and the toilets near Umejima on the down platform were removed.
17 March 2010 (Heisei 22): Departure melodies introduced on the Isesaki Line platforms.
17 March 2012 (Heisei 24): Station number "TS 13" introduced.
章节.Station layout:
The station is a ground-level station with three island platforms serving six tracks, and an over-track station building.
The Isesaki Line uses two island platforms serving four tracks. With direction-specific quadruple-track wiring, express, section-express, semi-express and section-semi-express services on the express tracks can transfer across the platform to local services on the local tracks.
Near the Umejima end of the platforms, single crossovers allow moves from the down local track to the express track and from the up express track to the local track; these are used by the TH Liner (which passes this station).
The Daishi Line platform is a bay platform serving two tracks. Normally the bay-side Track 1 is used, but owing to west-exit redevelopment and the demolition of Tosca Nishi-kan, Track 1 has been out of service since 1 February 2023, and for the time being all trains depart from and arrive at Track 2.
There is one ticket gate, with an intermediate gate at the entrance to the Daishi Line platform. Because Daishimae Station is unstaffed, ticket-checking functions for that station are handled at the Daishi Line transfer gate here.
Departure indicators are installed on the Isesaki Line platforms but not on the Daishi Line platform.
On 31 March 2005, elevators connecting the gates to each platform (at the Takenotsuka end) were completed, and barrier-free toilets were newly installed at gate level; simultaneously the toilets near Umejima on the down platform were removed.
From March 2010, departure melodies operated by the conductor's remote control were introduced on the Isesaki Line platforms (Tracks 3-6). The Daishi Line platform uses the departure melody "Passenger".
On 24 September 2022, a new west exit opened with newly installed elevators and escalators; the old west exit has undergone exterior-wall renovation.
章节.Platforms:
The line names use passenger-facing names ("Tobu Skytree Line" being a nickname).
In the timetable as of 6 June 2020, 37 up Isesaki Line trains departed this station in the hour beginning at 07:24. This is the highest frequency among private railways in the Kanto region and contributes greatly to easing rush-hour congestion.
The adjacent-station names on the station signage differ between the express and local tracks, as at Shin-Koshigaya and Soka. At the other express stops, Koshigaya and Kita-Senju, only local-track names are listed: at Koshigaya because down semi-express and section-semi-express services stop at all stations, and at Kita-Senju because all platforms handle local services.
The Umejima end of the Daishi Line track (Track 2) connected to the Nishi-Arai factory, which lay south of the station, until March 2004. The factory moved to the Minami-Kurihashi factory in April the same year and closed.
The 0 km post of the Daishi Line lies beside the track on the side not facing the Daishi Line platform on Track 2; that point is the center of the station.
章节.Standing-eat ramen: On the down Isesaki Line platform (Tracks 3 and 4) there is a standing-eat ramen shop called "Nishi-Arai Ramen".
章节.Usage: In fiscal 2022, the station had an average of 58,836 boarding and alighting passengers daily. This figure excludes passengers transferring between the Isesaki Line and the Daishi Line. It ranks seventh among Isesaki Line stations, after Kasukabe. Since fiscal 2002, redevelopment has been carried out at the west exit, and through services to the Hanzomon Line have become available, so ridership has been on an upward trend.
章节.Surrounding area:
Nishi-Arai Daishi (Soji-ji), one of the three major Daishi temples in the Kanto region, lies about 1 km to the west; Daishimae Station on the Daishi Line is the nearest station. In March 2004 an elevator was newly installed at the east exit, and minor renovations to the Tosca Higashi-kan and former Nishi-kan shop areas allowed 24-hour passage through the east-west free passage using in-store elevators.
Ring Road 7 (Tokyo Metropolitan Route 318, Kanpachi-dori) crosses the tracks toward Takenotsuka and Daishimae on the north side (Nishi-Arai Overpass). Around the west exit, redevelopment centered on the site of the former Nisshinbo Tokyo factory was carried out (Nishi-Arai Nouvel). Along the free passage, besides Tosca-series kiosks, there are a FamilyMart, QB House, a Tobu Top Tours Nishi-Arai branch, and a Japan Post Bank ATM. The west exit is a large bus terminal.
Mixed-use urban redevelopment has been carried out around Nishi-Arai Eitai-cho.
章节.Bus routes: Route buses, including the Adachi Ward community bus "Harukaze", arrive and depart here. Operators are four companies: Tobu Bus Central, the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation, Kokusai Kogyo Bus, and Hitachi Jidosha Kotsu.
章节.Nishi-Arai Station West Exit: ※ Late-night bus route Late 31 (Tobu Bus Central) runs from Oji Station via Ring Road 7 to Nishi-Arai Station West Exit.
章节.Nishi-Arai Overpass: ※ In front of the former Nishi-Arai Police Station, on Ring Road 7, a 7-minute walk from the west exit. Before the west-exit rotary was built, most Kokusai Kogyo routes reversed here.
章节.Nishi-Arai Station East Exit: ※ Bus stop 1 is under the Nishi-Arai Overpass on Ring Road 7; bus stop 2 is to the right after descending the east-exit stairs, in front of Tosca.
章节.Other: The place name "Nishi-Arai", from which the station takes its name, is a single word and is not a compound with the prefix "Nishi" (west). The kanji alone do not reveal whether it is a compound, but the difference appears in the romanized notation on station and in-train stop lists. On Tobu Railway, station names prefixed with a direction are hyphenated, such as Kita-senju and Shin-koshigaya, whereas Nishi-Arai is written without a hyphen as Nishiarai.

On 31 March 2005, elevators connecting the gates to each platform (at the Takenotsuka end) were completed, and barrier-free toilets were newly installed at gate level; simultaneously the toilets near Umejima on the down platform were removed.
From March 2010, departure melodies operated by the conductor's remote control were introduced on the Isesaki Line platforms (Tracks 3-6). The Daishi Line platform uses the departure melody "Passenger".
On 24 September 2022, a new west exit opened with newly installed elevators and escalators; the old west exit has undergone exterior-wall renovation.

Platforms
The line names use passenger-facing names ("Tobu Skytree Line" being a nickname).
In the timetable as of 6 June 2020, 37 up Isesaki Line trains departed this station in the hour beginning at 07:24. This is the highest frequency among private railways in the Kanto region and contributes greatly to easing rush-hour congestion.
The adjacent-station names on the station signage differ between the express and local tracks, as at Shin-Koshigaya and Soka. At the other express stops, Koshigaya and Kita-Senju, only local-track names are listed: at Koshigaya because down semi-express and section-semi-express services stop at all stations, and at Kita-Senju because all platforms handle local services.
The Umejima end of the Daishi Line track (Track 2) connected to the Nishi-Arai factory, which lay south of the station, until March 2004. The factory moved to the Minami-Kurihashi factory in April the same year and closed.
The 0 km post of the Daishi Line lies beside the track on the side not facing the Daishi Line platform on Track 2; that point is the center of the station.

Standing-eat ramen
On the down Isesaki Line platform (Tracks 3 and 4) there is a standing-eat ramen shop called "Nishi-Arai Ramen".

Usage
In fiscal 2022, the station had an average of 58,836 boarding and alighting passengers daily. This figure excludes passengers transferring between the Isesaki Line and the Daishi Line. It ranks seventh among Isesaki Line stations, after Kasukabe. Since fiscal 2002, redevelopment has been carried out at the west exit, and through services to the Hanzomon Line have become available, so ridership has been on an upward trend.

Surrounding area
Nishi-Arai Daishi (Soji-ji), one of the three major Daishi temples in the Kanto region, lies about 1 km to the west; Daishimae Station on the Daishi Line is the nearest station. In March 2004 an elevator was newly installed at the east exit, and minor renovations to the Tosca Higashi-kan and former Nishi-kan shop areas allowed 24-hour passage through the east-west free passage using in-store elevators.
Ring Road 7 (Tokyo Metropolitan Route 318, Kanpachi-dori) crosses the tracks toward Takenotsuka and Daishimae on the north side (Nishi-Arai Overpass). Around the west exit, redevelopment centered on the site of the former Nisshinbo Tokyo factory was carried out (Nishi-Arai Nouvel). Along the free passage, besides Tosca-series kiosks, there are a FamilyMart, QB House, a Tobu Top Tours Nishi-Arai branch, and a Japan Post Bank ATM. The west exit is a large bus terminal.
Mixed-use urban redevelopment has been carried out around Nishi-Arai Eitai-cho.

Other
The place name "Nishi-Arai", from which the station takes its name, is a single word and is not a compound with the prefix "Nishi" (west). The kanji alone do not reveal whether it is a compound, but the difference appears in the romanized notation on station and in-train stop lists. On Tobu Railway, station names prefixed with a direction are hyphenated, such as Kita-senju and Shin-koshigaya, whereas Nishi-Arai is written without a hyphen as Nishiarai.
